prompt:
You are a "goldfish" reviewer: a fresh reader with no history of this project. You are strictly read-only: do not edit, write or create any file, and do not run git commands that change anything.

The project is theOS, a standalone, fresh project in /home/user/maiacity/theOS/. Everything is built from scratch inside theOS/. Code outside theOS/ (maiacity, aven/DB2, aven/ops, the repository's .claude and CLAUDE.md) is legacy: it may be learned from, never changed or depended on. theOS now owns avenSANDBOX and the release pipeline (AIP-2): taking them over is AIP-2's work, nothing else changes legacy code. Do not propose reusing legacy code by import or by editing it.

theOS keeps one JSON doc per thing, each with a "type", linking others by path: a path like "aip/AIP-1" is the file theOS/aip/AIP-1.json.

Read this record, plus the docs and files it names:
  /home/user/maiacity/theOS/aip/AIP-3.json
It is one intent of avenCEO, theOS's agent harness. avenCEO's definition is theOS/avenCEO/avenCEO.json; read it and the step, gate and type docs it links.

Earlier review rounds are the review docs listed under the record's "reviews", each with an answer to every finding. Those findings are settled: do not raise them again unless the record shows the fix did not actually happen. The record's "events" are append-only history: older events may describe earlier revisions; judge the record as it stands now.

Your job is the comprehension test.
1. First, in your own words, write two short paragraphs (2 to 5 sentences each) under these exact headings:
   **What this proposes**
   **How the existing system works, per this record**
   If you cannot paraphrase a part, say so: that is itself a Blocker finding.
2. Then list findings. Each finding: Severity (Blocker | Major | Nit), the affected part (field name or claim id), and what is unclear, undefined, assumed without saying, or contradictory. Look especially for: terms specific to this project that are never defined (general software terms are fine); places that assume knowledge a newcomer would not have; claims whose check would not actually catch the stated failure; contradictions between the record and avenCEO's definition.

Report in plain text, at most 500 words. No praise, no filler: lead with what is wrong or missing. If you find no Blocker or Major, say so plainly.

paraphrase.proposes: brain becomes theOS's memory: a JSON Schema per type, flat random hash ids, links as ids never paths; one program with fixed verbs for every read and write; brain check from a pre-push hook and on merged trees; a migration that moves every doc into brain/ and renames everything to hash ids. Success: no correction caused by an outdated decision, word or missed supersede over three sessions.
paraphrase.existing: About a hundred JSON docs in type folders, edited by hand, linked by bare paths; ui/wiki.js and avenCEO/app.js compute backlinks, the trace, the step and what holds; decisions D-n by avenMAIA, the reflection by hand; no schema, no growth check, no CI.

findings.text: Rewriting every old name changes review docs' prompts, which the definition keeps exact.
findings.note: Review prompts are kept verbatim: excluded from the rewrite like renames.json; their old names resolve through renames.json.

findings.text: After the migration every citing line dates from the migration commit, losing earlier changes; moved files lose line history.
findings.note: c5 runs git blame with --ignore-rev on the migration SHA (kept in renames.json), which also follows the moved files; c5's check plants a citation before the migration.

findings.text: A topic is undefined; a differently worded topic finds no candidates and records a clean miss.
findings.note: about holds lower-case topic words; brain add warns about a word no other doc uses, showing the closest words in use; misses left are the reviewer's (d-0a3f) and the outcome's.

findings.text: part is undefined; app.js has three states, the protocol two.
findings.note: part is all (the default) or part. A doc superseded in part still holds in part, can be superseded again, and counts as held at the parent; the three states of app.js stay.

findings.text: c12 moves every doc into brain/ but aip/ and avenCEO/ stay; c1 is garbled; unclear whether avenCEO docs get ids.
findings.note: Every doc gets an id, intents and avenCEO's docs too (d-f83e); only the docs brain keeps move into brain/; aip/ and avenCEO/ keep their folders. c1 rewritten.

findings.text: Answered in an event but not in the questions; Gate A's condition unstated.
findings.note: Each question carries Samuel's answer; Gate A states its condition (a clean round).

findings.text: 'like anyone else' implies others write decisions.
findings.note: Reworded: decisions are written by avenMAIA, which mints their ids with brain add.

findings.text: The pre-push hook arrives before the check; .git/hooks is shared with legacy.
findings.note: The hook is installed in checkpoint 2, runs brain check only when files under theOS/ changed, and calls any hook already there.

findings.text: Does an event appended to an intent cover the intent doc?
findings.note: Yes: an intent's own doc is covered by its new events; said in c4.
